summary.name: 3 Ways to Minimize the Impact of High Severity Incidents
summary.one_liner: A DevOps.com article offering three practices for reducing the impact of high severity incidents: an incident manager on-call role, identifying critical services, and chaos engineering.
keywords: single point of contact during outages
use_cases: setting up an incident manager on-call rotation
reducing time to resolve production outages
identifying which services are most critical
making the case for reliability investment
summary.what_it_does: The article argues that high severity incidents should be resolved quickly and safely, citing a claim that a single hour of downtime can cost over $100,000. It proposes an incident manager on-call (IMOC) role responsible for a SEV from detection through closure, providing one point of contact and aiming to lower MTTR. It recommends assessing the reliability of the top critical services so teams know where failures would cause SEVs. It also describes chaos engineering as planned experiments that reveal system weaknesses before they cause incidents.
notable: Incident manager on-call (IMOC) role covering detection, diagnosis, mitigation, prevention and closure
Recommends assessing the top critical services for reliability
Frames chaos engineering as proactive planned experiments
caveats: Downtime cost figure is attributed to a third-party research firm and is not independently verified on the page
Article is opinion and practice advice, not a tool or product; no implementation details are given
